answer_text:
Using polar coordinates in \(\mathbb{R}^n\),

\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{1}{(1+|x|)^N}\,dx
=
\omega_{n-1}\int_0^\infty \frac{r^{n-1}}{(1+r)^N}\,dr,
\]

where \(\omega_{n-1}\) is the surface area of the unit sphere \(S^{n-1}\).

Near \(r=0\), the integrand behaves like \(r^{n-1}\), which is integrable. For convergence, we only need to check \(r\to\infty\). As \(r\to\infty\),

\[
\frac{r^{n-1}}{(1+r)^N} \sim r^{n-1-N}.
\]

The integral \(\int^\infty r^{n-1-N}\,dr\) converges exactly when

\[
n-1-N < -1,
\]

so

\[
N>n.
\]

At \(N=n\), the integrand behaves like \(1/r\), which diverges logarithmically.

Thus the integral converges for real \(N\) if and only if

\[
\boxed{N>n\quad\text{(so if }N\text{ must be an integer, the minimum is }N=n+1)}.
\]
